notes.title: Hot Tree Bile Shops and Wintery Improvements
notes.content:
Another development update showing off some more WIP features! Have a watch of the video:
[previewyoutube=xenZDjXWSa0;full][/previewyoutube]
A mug of piping hot tree bile, who can forget its taste. You will not be able to. It is memorable. I know, these days people say that you can "just get it in a can" and that it's "just as good as straight from the tree stumps disgusting mouth." Those people are liars and they are scoundrels. You've got to drink it straight from the source:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/63b286964e55e3352e0948731fc6719eb5889fa6.png

Mmm. There's nothing quite like it.

Aside from building new shops that will placate the thirst of your zoo visitors in the middle of winter, winter itself is looking very pretty these days:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/a44ec5d68179423ab6bafa93b070ba07316534c5.png

Snow falls and builds up all around, the zoo visitors come bundled in coats, hats and scarfs, and so on. It looks really nice at 60fps.

More updates coming soon!
- Matt

notes.title: The Electric Chair and The Joy Drinker Statue
notes.content:
Here's a brand new update about The Eldritch Zookeeper's development:
[previewyoutube=6GWo-zw3d-k;full][/previewyoutube]
There's a brand new electricity grid system in The Eldritch Zookeeper:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/50c541cf4cda0362d55908474868d6dbb2e701c1.png
See those yellow lines? Those are electric power lines running between all the lampposts and all the electric buildables in your zoo.

Where does the power come from? 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/872607d5b237e2772023aab4660a288c715aba9b.png
All those happy zoo visitors are now a non-polluting power source for your zoo expansion! Congratulations to each and every one of them. Whenever they walk beneath the statue's open hand, their joy is turned into useful charge, and will zip about your electrical grid to wherever it needs to go.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/1e8f31a6237454e464c9ae4a43451b9d4ca079d4.png
The Electric Chair is the first new powered device that needs a strong electrical input. Recharge your staff automatons in what we really, really hope is a non-painful way of getting them busy after depleting their battery. There's no reliable evidence that the automatons feel pain and there's certainly no way they can complain about it if they do, so it's fine.

The automatons can also hold scythes and cut the grass for you! How helpful of them.

Check out that video for more info! More updates on the way, stay tuned...
- Matt

notes.title: Stone Paths, Grass and a Big Scythe
notes.content:
Here's a brand new update about The Eldritch Zookeeper's development:
[previewyoutube=LNAtJuTIFVI;full][/previewyoutube]
Stone paths! At long last. And they look so gooood.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/155670053953daf11520a980405ef425e8d2bff6.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/46b5cbd7bb7d45283f8faba843ffc0394c415266.png
It's taken a lot of tweaking to get the construction of the stone paths feeling right. You sort of 'paint' the path onto the ground as you run about, and that looks and sounds really satisfying. I'd like to add a few different path variations that you can choose between, and will change the look of your zoo pretty drastically.

Grass that grows is the other Big New Thing, and if you let your zoo get a bit out of control in that regard, it's a bit of a mess:

Check out that video to see all of that in motion! More updates on the way, stay tuned...
- Matt

notes.title: Magical (and Helpful) Automatons
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/3fe55edd303ee352f539e17835bb1ee854989b1b.gif

Doo doo doo doo (that's the sound I think it makes to itself as it runs along.)

I've added staff you can hire to help you with your zookeeping, they're these big battery-with-legs-and-arms-and-a-lantern-as-a-head things, and they're pretty helpful:

[previewyoutube=JeJs5hBSzCs;full][/previewyoutube]
The gameplay issue I allude to that video is that maintaining big zoos was increasingly difficult, the larger they got. It wasn't hard to build a big zoo, it was keeping it going that was challenging. At a certain point there were just too many monsters needing food, too many litter bins needing emptying, just too many jobs for one player to manage. Because, remember, if a monster goes hungry, after a little while they get agitated, then angry, and they start breaking stuff and killing everything they can get their teeth/claws/tentacles into.

But with staff to do all the busywork for you, you can keep expanding and building, and investing in new monsters and redesigning your zoo without having to do a full-zoo circuit to keep everything going. Of course, you have to invest in these staff first and scale up the right way, but the automatons are already really helping.

As I say in the video, there's a few more things I think these automatons can help with, and I'd like to make them upgradable and more efficient. But it's a good start!

More updates coming soon.

notes.title: Mad Science!
notes.content:
Science.

Sure, it's been around since the enlightenment, but that was ages ago. If you're bored of physics, chemistry - and who isn't? Who wants to study rocks and rock-adjacent stuff? - Then perhaps it's time to look to the fringes? Alchemical Black Science! That's the really exciting stuff, and it's even more exciting because it's forbidden.

The bonus is you don't have to worry about all that pesky 'ethics board' nonsense. Watch the update video all about the new research lab:
[previewyoutube=aeDp8B5R6aE;full][/previewyoutube]
Brains floating in a jar do all the work for us, how kind of them.

Adding a tech-tree full of research options has been a long time coming, and now the cackling mad scientist has arrived at last, I can continue to fill it up with all sorts of interesting additions, and 'New Stuff'. My plan is to first make the research tree of options broad (as in, at the very start of any game you can choose a wide array of ) and then deep (some research items need to be unlocked before others, and these can be chained together.) Do you 'go deep' on one particularly promising looking vein of research? Or do you instead dabble here and there in the shallow end?

Whatever you research; new monsters, new shops, upgrades and enhancements, they're going to improve your Zoo's Visitor Satisfaction Rating that we talked about last time.

One advantage of having a broad tech-tree is that you can start off a zoo in a very different way. There's no 'best build order', or at least, there'll be quite a number of viable options.

notes.title: What Makes A Monster Zoo Good?
notes.content:
What makes a zoo good? What makes a zoo bad? Obviously, when it comes to monster zoos, having some sort of fence-like-structure between zoo visitors and the terrible creatures is a good start, but what about the rest of the zoo? How important are litter bins, and illumination, and having enough food and drink shops, and bathroom cleanliness, and queue lengths for all these services? Well, they are important! Cutting corners is frowned upon for most zookeepers, and surely even more for cursed ones.

[previewyoutube=ifq1AFlQHxY;full][/previewyoutube]

I hope you enjoy what is my longest and most in-depth development video yet! I think it gives the start of a good overview of what will make The Eldritch Zookeeper a deep, rich and super-rewarding game to play.

Game Design Philosophy Time:
Here's an opinion I have about certain management/tycoon games: sometimes, they're not really very deep or challenging.

Let me explain: there are some games where you build a Thing (a theme park, a hospital, a school, or whatever else) where all you do as a player is to build some things, wait for money to accumulate, maybe research some new things, build those things with the money, and repeat until there's nothing more to build. Don't get me wrong; lots of games with that sort of 'gameplay loop' are entertaining and relaxing, and it's satisfying to build a Thing the way you want to.

Still, something I want to accomplish in The Eldritch Zookeeper is to have the zoo simulation push back on you in different ways. I want there to be situations where certain aspects of the zoo you're building get stressed, or have more weight put on them, to test whether the zoo can handle them. The Zoo Satisfaction Rating system I talk through in the video is how I'm measuring where a zoo is at, where it's struggling and whether it's improving or floundering.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/55238058991e684e2a52e0418363fdc5596c19ae.png

One nice aspect to the Zoo Satisfaction Rating is the way it looks at everything you do as a zookeeper. An important part of the Management/Tycoon subgenre is just letting the player build their Thing - in this case, a monster zoo - however they want. That sort of freedom and creative expression is something I want to encourage, and not squash by enforcing a certain Build Order, or 'Way You Have To Do Things'. If you want to focus on having lots of different, interesting monsters, the Zoo Satisfaction Rating system will reward you for that. If you want to focus on decorating your zoo nicely and making sure visitors get what they need, the rating system will do the same. Whatever you invest in will be rewarded, and at the same time there are the levers behind the scenes that can be tweaked to help you create a well-rounded zoo. And achieving that well-rounded zoo is, I hope, going to be a fun little puzzle for future players (like you!) to solve.

(Oh, and it's worth mentioning: if the player just wants to build for fun, in a relaxing way, without the game simulation seriously challenging the player, I absolutely want to allow the player to do that in a Free Build mode.)

Thanks for watching the video, I hope it makes you anticipate the game! Don't forget to wishlist the game, and if you want to join The Guild of Cursed Zookeepers simply visit: https://cranktrain.com/guild/ and follow the instructions. It's free! And in return you'll get Kristof, an exclusive playable zookeeper, as a Steam inventory item:

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/29396689/f854f9e0975256fd364c8d7e75f2785362f1fe7f.png

Thanks for watching and reading, I'll see you again soon!
- Matt

In summary:

• Smoothie Shops! After having Ice Cream shops in the game, now it's not just food, there's drinks too

• Bathrooms! If there's both food and drink in the game, it makes sense the visitors will need something else, right?

I think a next step of mine is to let the player know exactly how well they are doing with meeting the needs of the zoo guests. Some kind of global Visitor Satisfaction Rating that runs from 0 to 100, and perhaps some way of breaking that down into specific needs as well. How well you're doing with satisfying visitor's desires is going to correlate with how popular your zoo is... which of course leads to how many new visitors are going to turn up, which in turn powers your economic engine that lets you keep expanding and feeding your existing monsters so they don't go absolutely mad and kill everyone. <- This is the Game Loop, as they call it.

notes.title: Introducing the HypnoLlama! (And the HypnoLlama Queen!)
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29396689/0e1bd14626296007b866cea8e608de8e2709bc97.png

The Eldritch Zookeeper has a new trailer! To announce not one, but two new monsters to begrudgingly welcome to the monster zoo.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29396689/af6bce7c718673d01542c7d304718598306f332d.png

The HypnoLlama is a friendly-looking thing, indeed of all the monsters it appears, on first glance, to be almost normal. But looks can be deceiving, and that is why I never open my eyes, not ever. Because when the HypnoLlama gets agitated, maybe you've let it go hungry, or you've let it get too close to humans, or another monster is biting it - it has the tendency to grow angry and take over lesser minds. 'Lesser minds', in this case, are your zoo visitors. Hypnotised guests are filled with a thirst for destruction and, left unchecked, can quickly turn a nicely ordered zoo into a chaotic mess.

The HypnoLlama Queen, if you can imagine, is even worse. It... sort of looks like a bunch of HypnoLlama's have melted into each other? Perhaps that's exactly what has happened? On one hand, sure, it doesn't take up much space, and doesn't move around very much. But when angry it is an order of magnitude more dangerous than your everyday, run-of-the-mill HypnoLlama.

You'll also notice from the trailer a new voice! The definitely-evil skeleton who seems quite responsible for the zookeeper's cursed situation is played by actor Scott Gilmour. Some voice acting is a great new addition that I'm really excited about.

Oh! Also! We now have a Discord Server! We're a pleasant, chill group, so if that sounds like where you want to be, and to hear about the game as development continues, you can join us here: https://discord.gg/C6TdkaP

I'm still hard at work making this game, so follow along for more news:

notes.title: The 'Bigger Zoos' Update!
notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29396689/6b7e47f6855d4853209b7393ca0c5214e899a0b7.png
Hello! I'm Matt, I'm the lead developer and... well, I guess the only developer on The Eldritch Zookeeper. It's time to share an update on how things with the game have been progressing over the last while!

If you're new to The Eldritch Zookeeper, here's what you need to know:

     It's a game about managing a zoo, but the zoo is full of monsters.
     The game's not quite ready for release yet, but I'm working hard on it!
     It's going to be really fun.

So what's been going on the last six months of development? I've made a development update video that you can watch right now! It's here:

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/29396689/ac400eae88ecc2d23df3b88fe39c8c35071439bb.png

For those who don't like videos, here's the gist: I've been down in the slimy guts of the game's internals. It's greasy down there, but sometimes you've got to get your hands dirty.

There is now a proper Saving and Loading System in the game and this is a Big Deal™ - in-progress zoos can be returned to at a later point! You know, like, in video games.

Because I can easily load previously created zoos, I've been able to work on making sure that the game can be played well with lots of visitors and lots of monsters in it. I'm still working on the performance side of things, but it's coming along!

There's new zoo walls, or rather, fences around the perimeter! They're in the same cast-iron style as the zoo gate, and I think zoos look a lot prettier as a result.

A brand-new camera system! Smooth zooming, rotating, all the good stuff. Good game cameras aren't always the easiest thing to 

Feeding troughs! I like adding new things to the game that the player can actually build, and feeding troughs are a useful addition to monster enclosures. They keep the meat or the cosmic ooze (you know, whatever a monster might be hungry for) organised, because monsters might kick the food out of their pen. These monsters aren't the most intelligent things, but I wouldn't say that near them. I don't know what language they speak, and I don't know if they can read minds or not. What I do know is, they have a lot of teeth.

I'm excited to have returned from the aforementioned greasy-guts of the game, and back to creating new content. Exciting! If you haven't already, be sure to wishlist the game right here on Steam, and subscribe to the youtube channel (with Bell Button selected and all) to keep up-to-date with exciting development news!

 - Matt
